messages.subject: Using Multivariate Normal Distribution
parts:
I'm currently working on the sesame street model (ARM Ch23.4) and it
involves fitting a multivariate normal distribution. However, the way it
is set up in BUGS, it calls things like

ag[j,1:2] ~ dmnorm (mu.ag[1:2],Tau.ag[1:2,1:2])

where ag is a matrix[N,2]. I've tried using temp variables, but I've
found that it gets too messy since I can't assign variables in the model
block (i.e. a <- blah). However, a potential work around is to call it as

ag[j] ~ multi_normal(mu_ag,Tau_ag)

where ag[j] and mu_ag are both row vectors, but this isn't supported
either. Is there another way to do this or would it be worth adding
multi_normal for row_vectors y and mu?


Peter

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Using Multivariate Normal Distribution
parts:
It is probably worth adding. Actually, I think there is already C++ code that accepts a Nx2 matrix as the random variable, but it is not exposed. Anyway, for now, I think it would work if you just transposed the row vectors to column vectors in the call to the likelihood. Also, remember that BUGS parameterizes dmnorm() with the precision matrix, so to make it equivalent (and faster) with Stan, you should use multi_normal_prec().

Ben

Thanks for pointing that out--I've never used Bugs before so that's good to know.

I'm also having trouble trying to generate the 2x2 covariance matrix. I used the same priors as the Bugs code [Stan code below]. The code compiles, but when I run it, it throws an error like

data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> J;
  matrix[N,2] yt;

}

  matrix[2,2] Sigma_yt;

  cov_matrix[2] Sigma_ag;
  matrix[N,2] yt_hat;
  vector[J] a;
  vector[J] g;

  //data level
  Sigma_yt[1,1] <- pow(sigma_y,2);
  Sigma_yt[2,2] <- pow(sigma_t,2);
  Sigma_yt[1,2] <- rho_yt*sigma_y*sigma_t; 
  Sigma_yt[2,1] <- Sigma_yt[1,2];
  Tau_yt <- inverse(Sigma_yt);
  
  // group level
  Sigma_ag[1,1] <- pow(sigma_a,2);
  Sigma_ag[2,2] <- pow(sigma_g,2);
  Sigma_ag[1,2] <- rho_ag*sigma_a*sigma_g;
  Sigma_ag[2,1] <- Sigma_ag[1,2]; 
  Tau_ag <- inverse(Sigma_ag);

  for (j in 1:J) {
    a[j] <- ag[j,1];
    g[j] <- ag[j,2];
  }

  for (i in 1:N) {
    yt_hat[i,1] <- a[siteset[i]] + b * yt[i,2];
    yt_hat[i,2] <- g[siteset[i]] + d * z[i];
  }
}
model {
  //data level
  sigma_y ~ uniform (0, 100);              
  sigma_t ~ uniform (0, 100);                 
  rho_yt ~ uniform(-1, 1);
  d ~ normal (0, .001);
  b ~ normal (0, .001);

  //group level
  sigma_a ~ uniform (0, 100);
  sigma_g ~ uniform (0, 100);
  rho_ag ~ uniform(-1, 1);
  mu_ag[1] ~ normal (0, .001);
  mu_ag[2] ~ normal (0, .001);

  //data model
  for (i in 1:N)
    transpose(yt[i]) ~ multi_normal_prec(transpose(yt_hat[i]),Tau_yt);

  for (j in 1:J)
    transpose(ag[j]) ~ multi_normal_prec(mu_ag,Tau_ag);
}




Peter

On Friday, August 2, 2013 3:58:46 PM UTC-4, Peter Li wrote:
Thanks for pointing that out--I've never used Bugs before so that's good to know.

I'm also having trouble trying to generate the 2x2 covariance matrix. I used the same priors as the Bugs code [Stan code below]. The code compiles, but when I run it, it throws an error like

Error : Invalid value of Tau_yt: Error in function validate transformed params
 d: Tau_yt is not positive definite. Tau_yt(0,0) is -32.125953381363409.
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

The inverse() function should pretty much never be used, since it neither utilizes the fact that a covariance matrix is positive definite nor does a good job at preserving positive definiteness when the matrix is numerically near singular.

But if you are going to declare a cov_matrix as the transformed parameter, just pass the cov_matrix (not its inverse) to multi_normal() and don't worry about the problems with inverting.

Ben

> On Aug 2, 2013, at 12:13 PM, Peter Li wrote:
>
>> I'm currently working on the sesame street model (ARM Ch23.4) and it involves fitting a multivariate normal distribution. However, the way it is set up in BUGS, it calls things like
>>
>> ag[j,1:2] ~ dmnorm (mu.ag[1:2],Tau.ag[1:2,1:2])


>>
>> where ag is a matrix[N,2]. I've tried using temp variables, but I've found that it gets too messy since I can't assign variables in the model block (i.e. a <- blah). However, a potential work around is to call it as
>>
>> ag[j] ~ multi_normal(mu_ag,Tau_ag)
>>
>> where ag[j] and mu_ag are both row vectors, but this isn't supported either. Is there another way to do this or would it be worth adding multi_normal for row_vectors y and mu?

The best approach is this:

vector[2] ag[N];

vector[2] mu_ag;

cov_matrix[2] Tau_ag;

That way ag[n] is a vector, and everything should match the
signature.

The other way you could've done it is with an explicit transpose,
because ag[n]' is a vector if ag is a matrix[N,2].

We've been meaning to generalize the way multi_normal works
for ages but haven't gotten around to it yet.

- Bob
